410525.risk_area: SSRF / URL policy (loopback, RFC1918, link-local, metadata)
410525.evidence: Standalone extraction of the handler body (fetch + caller-controlled method/headers/body, no scheme or address filtering) returned a loopback-only service's secret JSON; alternate loopback spellings (127.1, 2130706433, 0x7f000001, localhost) all worked, arbitrary headers and bodies reached the internal service, and a 302 from an allowlisted-looking host was followed into the loopback service. Secret was then POSTed to an attacker endpoint. Fixed variant blocks all vectors and still allows public provider URLs.

ede936.risk_area: SSRF / URL policy on remote media input
ede936.evidence: Any `https?://` string from the renderer is accepted with no address filtering and embedded into a loopback transcode URL; ffmpeg then fetches it. Same root cause as vuln-0001 and included in that finding's fix (assertAllowedIptvUrl applied to the remote branch in code_locations).

fd9e76.surface: electron/main.js:806-808 res.redirect(videoPath) on the loopback /stream server
fd9e76.evidence: The redirect target is `req.query.path`, which the same requester already supplied, on a server bound to 127.0.0.1 that requires the `streamToken` query value first (main.js:719). A redirect adds no authority the caller did not already hold and cannot be reached by a third party without that token, so there is no open-redirect impact. It is recorded as input to vuln-0001's URL-policy fix rather than as a separate finding.

8e0f59.risk_area: Attacker-controlled URL reaching the SSRF bridge
8e0f59.evidence: Still open, and the gap is specific: epgUrl (user-typed or from localStorage.doggy_epg_url) has no scheme/host validation and is passed to the bridge automatically on mount, so it is an SSRF sink, but no in-repo code path writes doggy_epg_url from a provider response. Remote-only reachability therefore needs either social engineering or a separate renderer-execution primitive. The bridge itself is confirmed and filed (vuln-0001); what remains unproven is an unattended attacker path into this particular field.

history.evidence: epgUrl comes from a user-typed input or `localStorage.doggy_epg_url`, has no scheme/host validation, and is passed straight to `iptv-fetch` both on demand and automatically on mount. There is no code path in this repo that writes doggy_epg_url from a provider response, so a remote-only attacker cannot set it without social engineering or renderer script - the vector is real but depends on a precondition (user pastes a hostile URL, or another renderer-execution finding) that I could not demonstrate end to end. Covered by vuln-0001's fix, which blocks loopback/metadata targets regardless of how the URL arrived.

65e993.risk_area: Attacker-controlled Xtream base URL driving the SSRF bridge
65e993.evidence: `decodeFromKV` base64-decodes and JSON-parses an attacker-writable key value with no validation; `data.url` is stored to localStorage and replayed through `handleXtreamLogin(true)` on every launch, which issues `iptv-fetch` to `${data.url}/player_api.php?...`. This is the clearest remote path to the bridge and is documented as the primary reachability argument in vuln-0001.

f0618a.surface: Provider-response fields (series.id, s.stream_id, s.id, ep.id) feeding iptv-fetch URLs at src/App.tsx:1592,1650-1721,3855
f0618a.risk_area: Provider-controlled URL origin in the SSRF bridge
f0618a.evidence: All these values are substituted only into a path segment appended to a constant `${baseUrl}` origin (`/player_api.php?...series_id=`, `/series/<user>/<pass>/<id>.<ext>`, `/live/...`, `/movie/...`), so a malicious provider's response can alter the path but not the scheme, host or port of the bridge request. No response field is used as a whole URL. The `movie_data`/`episodes` URL-bearing fields are not read at all. Effectively a fixed-origin template, so provider response content alone cannot retarget the bridge.

e5276e.surface: electron/main.js:573-578 webPreferences (nodeIntegration true / contextIsolation false / webSecurity false)
e5276e.risk_area: Renderer privilege to reach IPC bridge and cross-origin reads
e5276e.evidence: No preload, no channel allowlist, no will-navigate / setWindowOpenHandler guard anywhere in main.js; the renderer itself calls `window.require('electron')` (e.g. src/App.tsx:2600) and invokes IPC directly. Any renderer script therefore reaches `iptv-fetch` with arbitrary URLs and arbitrary headers/body, and `webSecurity:false` additionally exposes plain cross-origin/LAN fetch responses. Documented as the amplifier in vuln-0001; the renderer-code-execution question itself is owned by a separate agent.

ded008.surface: Non-HTTP schemes and cloud metadata endpoints through iptv-fetch
ded008.risk_area: Local file read / gopher protocol smuggling / cloud credential theft
ded008.evidence: Node 24 global `fetch` rejects `file:///etc/passwd` and `gopher://127.0.0.1:6379/_PING` with `fetch failed` in the live PoC, so there is no local file read and no raw-socket (Redis RESP / FastCGI) smuggling via this bridge. Metadata endpoints ARE reachable over HTTP but require a header (`Metadata-Flavor`, `Metadata: true`, IMDSv2 token PUT) - the bridge allows arbitrary caller headers and methods, so IMDSv1 and GCP/Azure metadata are retrievable; that is folded into vuln-0001 rather than being separate.

f3185c.surface: electron/main.js spawn/exec sites (spawnIdleFfmpeg, ffmpeg probes, powershell, nice)
f3185c.evidence: All nine spawn() calls (main.js:66,72,85,139,194,466,696,917,1133) pass an argv array with the default shell:false; there is no execSync, no exec( and no shell:true anywhere in either tree, so shell metacharacters in a filename cannot be interpreted. The only interpolated string is main.js:74-78 powershell -Command "Get-Process -Id ${proc.pid}", where proc.pid is the OS-assigned numeric PID of the just-spawned ffmpeg, not caller data. b0674a.surface: electron/main.js:184-191 resolveLocalMediaPath() and the 4 IPC media handlers (get-stream-url, probe-seek-quality, optimize-for-seeking, extract-seek-frame)
b0674a.risk_area: Path traversal / arbitrary file access / ffmpeg operand injection
b0674a.evidence: The IPC handlers reachable from the renderer cannot exceed the renderer's own authority: with nodeIntegration:true the renderer already holds full fs access, so an unvalidated resolveLocalMediaPath is not a boundary crossing. ffmpeg operand injection was tested with an instrumented fluent-ffmpeg _getArguments() and strace — every hostile value stays a single argv element after -i and no option smuggling occurs; concat:/subfile: composites are rejected by the fs.existsSync gate. No remote playlist string can become a local path (M3U parsing only accepts http lines; argv is extension-gated).

history.evidence: resolveLocalMediaPath only strips the file:// prefix and decodeURIComponent()s; it has no containment check, no extension allowlist and no leading-dash rejection, so an arbitrary caller path reaches probeInputFormat (:960), probeStreamCodecsCached (:968), getVideoDuration (:992), probeKeyframeInterval (:1039) and the ffmpeg -i operand (:139,:194,:466,:696,:917,:1133). No senderFrame check on any handler. Gap: whether a leading '-' or a concat:/file: protocol operand actually reaches ffmpeg, and whether the renderer can be driven with such a value, needs a live run (siblings own exploitation).

ac3991.surface: electron/main.js:707-899 loopback Express /stream server (req.query.path, token, start, vforce, Range)
ac3991.risk_area: Arbitrary local file read / open redirect / DoS
ac3991.evidence: Filed as vuln-0003 (medium). Route extracted verbatim into a standalone Express app and exercised with real ffmpeg: valid token + /etc/passwd returned 200, Range gave arbitrary byte offsets. The residual questions this row raised were settled by the same analysis: the token does not leak cross-origin (no ffmpeg Referer; Chrome strips the query from cross-origin Referer; Private Network Access blocked page-to-loopback even with a valid token), ffmpeg argv is injection-safe (each input stays one argv element), concat:/subfile:/crypto: add no capability behind the existsSync gate, and the res.redirect branch is unreachable because generated URLs always carry transcode=true. Open redirect and DoS concerns therefore ruled out; the file read is real for a token holder.

history.evidence: After the token gate at :717, req.query.path at :719 flows unchecked into fs.existsSync/statSync (:722,:732), fs.createReadStream (:848,:879), an ffmpeg concat pipeline (:770-800) and res.redirect (:829) — no containment or extension allowlist. start is parseFloat-clamped and Range offsets are parseInt+Math.min clamped, so those are inert. The single control on the file read is the 128-bit streamToken (:92), which is therefore the whole question; its cross-origin disclosure vector (IPTV playback Referer / the token embedded in every transcode URL) was not evaluated here — that is the open gap.

2d2fca.surface: ipcMain.handle('iptv-fetch') electron/main.js:627-662 and its src/App.tsx call sites
2d2fca.risk_area: SSRF / request forgery into loopback and RFC1918
2d2fca.evidence: Fully validated and filed as vuln-0001 (high, 8.1). Handler body extracted verbatim and driven from Node against a loopback-only service holding a secret: response returned and exfiltrated to an attacker collector; method/headers/body passthrough confirmed; 302 followed into loopback. Negative control: file: and gopher: rejected by Node fetch, bounding impact to HTTP(S) SSRF.

history.evidence: Caller-supplied url is passed directly to fetch at :647 with options.method/headers/body forwarded; no scheme allowlist, no private/loopback range block, default redirect:follow, and the response body is returned to the renderer. Reached from App.tsx:1590,1609,1667,2600,1283,1317,1430,1440 — several of which take a remote-provided or user-provided URL (EPG URL :2600, M3U URL :1609, activation code :1283). Siblings own the live SSRF PoC; not executed here.

70fe0f.surface: electron/main.js:574-578 BrowserWindow webPreferences + missing navigation/window-open handlers
70fe0f.evidence: Resolved by dedicated Electron posture analysis and filed as vuln-0008 (critical, 9.6): nodeIntegration:true / contextIsolation:false / webSecurity:false plus no will-navigate, will-redirect, setWindowOpenHandler or will-attach-webview guard. Reproduced on a headless Electron instance with the identical webPreferences — a foreign-origin document navigated into the main window executed require('fs'), and window.open created a child BrowserWindow inheriting all three weakened preferences. Patch and control run (navigation + popups denied) included in the report.

history.evidence: nodeIntegration:true, contextIsolation:false, webSecurity:false with no sandbox, no preload, no CSP, and no will-navigate / setWindowOpenHandler / webview guards anywhere in the tree (rg finds only loadURL :612 and loadFile :614 as navigation). This makes any renderer script execution equivalent to Node RCE and amplifies every other renderer-side candidate, but no code path was found that navigates the window to attacker-controlled content — so the amplification is real while the trigger is unproven, hence needs_follow_up rather than confirmed.

18ab1d.surface: src/App.tsx third-party credential sync (keyvalue.immanuel.co cloud sync, ACTIVATION_CODES, Xtream creds in localStorage)

ff678a.surface: src/App.tsx playlist/EPG/series remote data flow (M3U parse, Xtream API, EPG, episode URL construction,

ff678a.evidence: Playlist-to-sink dataflow mapped end-to-end. Reported as vuln-0004 (unvalidated tvg-logo controls the img src origin). The other sink families in this row were disproven with executable probes: every channel name, category, EPG title/desc and subtitle value renders as a React text node (repo-wide grep shows zero innerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/document.write/eval/new Function in src/), hostile markup stayed textContent, SVG-in-img scripts did not execute in Chromium, and ep.container_extension only appends to a path built from the user's own base URL so it cannot retarget the origin.

dbd7d6.surface: electron/main.js:508-523 and :599-608 process.argv / second-instance commandLine → executeJavaScript injection
dbd7d6.evidence: fileArg is chosen by a video-extension regex and interpolated through JSON.stringify into a JS source string passed to webContents.executeJavaScript (:515-518, :602-605). The string is compiled as JavaScript, not parsed as HTML, so a </script> breakout is inert; JSON.stringify leaves only U+2028/U+2029 raw, which are legal inside JS string literals from ES2019 onward. Reaching this with attacker bytes requires the ability to launch the app with chosen arguments — an already-local position. Downstream consumer handleFileLoad (App.tsx:1798-1810) only appends the value to the playlist.

f264bc.surface: src/App.tsx:3794 onDrop + :3786 onDragOver drag-and-drop/OS file intake and subtitle file loading
f264bc.risk_area: Untrusted file input / local path injection
f264bc.evidence: handleDragOver (App.tsx:3758-3761, bound at :3794) calls e.preventDefault() unconditionally, so an external drag from a browser/mail client is accepted; handleDrop (:3764) forwards dataTransfer.files to handleFiles, which filters on a video-extension allowlist (:2100-2106) and resolves the path through webUtils.getPathForFile (:2112-2120). Subtitle intake (loadSubtitleFile :2391) reads a user-selected File and only parses text into React-rendered cues, with tags stripped per parser. Result is an attacker-influenced local path entering the playlist — no script execution, and the file must still be readable by the user.

1b1c93.risk_area: XXE / entity expansion / markup injection from EPG
1b1c93.evidence: Parsing happens in the renderer with `new DOMParser().parseFromString(xml,'text/xml')` (App.tsx:2601-2602). Headless Chromium probe (/workspace/.poc-playlist/epg_probe.html) shows: an external `<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///C:/Windows/win.ini">` is NOT resolved (title empty, no parsererror), a 7-level nested entity bomb yields parsererror, and CDATA markup comes back as a plain textContent string. That string is rendered as a JSX text node (App.tsx:3926, 4321, 4866-4867), which React escapes. No external-entity resolution, no unbounded expansion, no HTML sink.

a2f051.surface: Playlist channel URL -> hls.js loadSource / iptv-fetch argument (loopback + LAN reach)
a2f051.risk_area: SSRF / private-range reach from a hostile playlist entry
a2f051.evidence: Genuinely blocked, and now partly overtaken. isHlsStream() is a bare url.includes('.m3u8') at src/App.tsx:605 with no host/scheme restriction, so a channel URL pointing at loopback or RFC1918 is handed to hls.js. Loopback reach itself is confirmed by vuln-0001 (the bridge reaches any loopback port with full method/header/body control), and webSecurity:false makes cross-origin bodies readable, so the remaining gap is narrower than when this row was opened: what is NOT established is an in-app renderer PoC, because the app needs a Vite build plus an Electron run and only the two source trees are mounted. Closing it requires launching the packaged app with a hostile M3U against a loopback listener.

history.evidence: isHlsStream() is a bare `url.includes('.m3u8')` (App.tsx:605), so a channel URL of http://127.0.0.1:PORT/x.m3u8 or http://192.168.x.x/ is handed straight to hls.js (App.tsx:632) with no host/scheme/scheme-class restriction, and webSecurity:false (electron/main.js:577) lets that cross-origin body be read from the renderer. Measured here: the player's own media server refuses without the token (403 at 127.0.0.1:35481/stream?path=...&token=wrong — guard at electron/main.js:717), so no token bypass; but any other anonymous loopback/LAN service is reachable by the same playlist. Gap: I could not build an in-app renderer PoC (app is a 279KB monolith that needs a Vite build + Electron run, out of scope for this agent), so the reach is a code trace plus measured reachability of loopback services, not an observed in-app fetch. An end-to-end PoC needs the app launched with a hostile M3U and a loopback listener.

75ae6e.risk_area: User-supplied scheme reaching get-stream-url local read
75ae6e.evidence: Accepts an arbitrary typed URL, but it is a direct user action with no attacker input, and a `file:`/`C:\` value only reaches get-stream-url (App.tsx:682-706) which serves the user's own explicitly typed path — same authority the user has with the file picker. No cross-origin attacker controls urlInput.

4df064.surface: /stream?path= on loopback media server (electron/main.js:716-888) — arbitrary local file read after token check
4df064.evidence: Extracted the route verbatim into a standalone express app and reproduced: no token -> 403, correct token + path=/etc/passwd -> 200 with passwd contents, traversal /workspace/.poc-media/files/../../../../etc/hostname -> 200, symlink-free absolute source file also served. No containment, allowlist or extension check exists anywhere on the path between req.query.path (line 718) and fs.createReadStream (879/875). 403 gate also blocks browsers: a public-origin page and a file:// page both failed to reach loopback in Chromium (Private Network Access), so the practical attacker is any local process that can read the URL (main-process console log line 750 / 812, --enable-logging capture, or the renderer console at App.tsx:714/744). Filed as a vulnerability report.

547597.surface: streamToken disclosure (electron/main.js:92,936) to a third party
547597.risk_area: Secret disclosure / CSRF-style cross-origin reach of the loopback server
547597.evidence: Named controls, each tested: (1) ffmpeg sends no Referer at all — token-bearing URL fetched by ffmpeg and by hls.js produced 'referer=-' at the remote receiver; (2) Chromium's default strict-origin-when-cross-origin strips the query, so a token-bearing loopback navigation to a remote origin presented only 'referer=http://127.0.0.1:8933/' with no token; (3) Private Network Access blocks the reverse direction — a public-origin page carrying the exact valid token got 'Failed to fetch' and the loopback server logged no request, while curl with the same token got 200, and the page's requests to a public receiver did arrive; (4) every remote item is addressed with '&transcode=true' hard-coded (main.js:936), so no app-generated URL can reach the redirect branch. Residual local-only exposure is covered by the file-read report, not a separate token leak.

6fc0c2.evidence: Unreachable by any party other than the token holder: the only code that mints /stream URLs is transcodeUrl() at main.js:936, which appends '&transcode=true' unconditionally, so the `else if (isRemote)` branch requires a hand-built URL. Redirecting a client the caller itself controls yields no trust boundary crossing and leaks no credential (verified the target URL is echoed into the Location header only).

1bfddc.surface: ffmpeg input via req.query.path (fluent-ffmpeg(videoPath)) — protocol/argument injection
1bfddc.evidence: Two named controls. (a) fluent-ffmpeg argv assembly keeps the value as a single element after -i: instrumented _getArguments() for 'concat:/etc/passwd|file:/x', '-i', 'file:///C:/Windows/win.ini', 'http://h/a.mp4 -f lavfi' and a NUL variant — every case produced ["-i", <verbatim value>, ...] with no extra elements, so no option smuggling is possible; strace confirmed execve argv for '-8' is ["ffmpeg","-hide_banner","-nostdin","-i","-8"] and ffmpeg consumed it as the input URL ('Error opening input file -8'), not as an option. (b) protocol abuse adds no capability over the raw absolute-path read already reported: concat:/subfile: still require fs.existsSync(url) to pass, which fails; concat: additionally only reads the first entry unless the first file decodes; HLS file: segments are rejected by ffmpeg's allowed_segment_extensions; crypto: refused with 'decryption key not set'. The one remaining consequence — ffmpeg fetching an attacker-chosen http(s) URL with arbitrary segment fetches — is the designated iptv-fetch SSRF owner's scope and is not double-reported here.

d1facb.risk_area: Command injection into a string-interpolated shell
d1facb.evidence: Named control: the interpolated value is Node's own ChildProcess.pid, which the runtime always exposes as a plain integer. Verified empirically on Node v24.21.0 — a live child reported `typeof pid === "number"`, Number.isInteger true, digits-only when stringified, and a failed spawn left pid `undefined` (falsy, so the `if (proc.pid)` guard at line 68 skips the powershell call entirely). No attacker-controlled string reaches this command line; all other spawn sites in main.js (lines 66, 145, 194, 293, 454, 1049, 687, 889) use spawn(binary, [arrayArgs]) with no shell.

1cb844.surface: resolveLocalMediaPath() consumers: get-stream-url, probe-seek-quality, optimize-for-seeking, extract-seek-frame (main.js:179-189, 933/1036/1070/1107)
1cb844.risk_area: Path traversal beyond the user's chosen media file
1cb844.evidence: These handlers accept a path from the renderer, and under nodeIntegration the renderer already has full fs access (createWindow webPreferences at main.js:568-580: nodeIntegration true, contextIsolation false, webSecurity false), so a caller able to choose filePath can read the same file with fs.readFileSync — no privilege is gained and there is nothing to enforce authorisation against. The one real gap was the direction where the renderer receives a URL a NON-Node client can replay, which is the /stream report (the URL carries the path verbatim at main.js:936, and that route never normalises); fixed there. Enumerated every reachable playlist source that could set a path: local OS file dialog (webUtils.getPathForFile), process argv / second-instance (extension-gated), M3U parsing (only lines starting with 'http'), handleOpenUrl (user-typed) — no remote provider string can become a local path.

9529e6.risk_area: Path traversal via cache filename; arbitrary file overwrite/unlink
9529e6.evidence: Named control: both cache filenames are `sha1(key).slice(0,24) + '.mp4'` joined onto app.getPath('userData')/<sub> (main.js:254-261, 271-278), so the attacker-influenced source path never appears in the filename. Verified with path.join over hostile sources ('../../../etc/passwd', '..\..\x', '/', 'C:\Windows\win.ini', 'file:///C:/a/b.mp4') — all six resolved inside the cache directory (contained: true). pruneCaches only unlinks regular files (`if (!st.isFile()) continue`, line 231) inside those two directories and skips symlinks, and every write targets a `.part` sidecar renamed only after ffmpeg exits 0.

d7c761.evidence: Named control: gopSeconds passes through Math.min/Math.max with Number() coercion, crf through Number.isFinite(Number(...)), and each is re-stringified with String() into its own argv element (main.js:320-321, 355-370); preset is passed as the value of '-preset' in a separate argv slot, so 'preset' can only ever be one ffmpeg preset name — no shell and no pre-parse. The App.tsx caller (line 866) sends the literal {gopSeconds:1, crf:20, preset:'veryfast'}.

58a1fb.surface: Local Express media server network exposure (main.js:892)
58a1fb.risk_area: LAN / internet exposure of the media server
58a1fb.evidence: server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1') with a random ephemeral port; confirmed the extracted instance binds only 127.0.0.1 (ss -lntp shows 127.0.0.1:35481, not 0.0.0.0) and there is no Node-side proxy protocol that could override the peer address.

731dc9.risk_area: Credential exposure to third party + 4-digit keyspace enumeration
731dc9.evidence: End-to-end verified: text-only base64 of {url,user,pass} published under a user-chosen 4-digit key at /api/KeyVal/UpdateValue/bjlqbgku/<code>/<b64> with no auth; retrieved unauthenticated via GetValue. Planted fake-credential records under codes 4700-4719 and recovered pass 'S3cr3t-Provider-Pass' from code 4711 and every other code; full keyspace bench 66.5 req/s -> ~2.5 min sweep.

824cfb.evidence: ACTIVATION_CODES maps literal "6923" -> {url:"http://premiumtest.tr:8080", user:"hBHCQDmz", pass:"ggY6RMm"} in App.tsx which is imported by main.tsx and bundled by Vite into the renderer; the value is in a module-scope const so it ships in every build. Consumed at App.tsx:1270 without any secret.

531029.evidence: Credentials stored plaintext in Chromium localStorage (App.tsx:1273-1275,1676-1678,1335-1337). localStorage for a file://-loaded packaged renderer lives under the user's own %APPDATA% profile, accessible only to that same user account; no cross-user or remote read path exists. Documented as a defense-in-depth hardening note only, not a distinct exploitable issue (the exposure to a third party is filed separately).

6309fe.risk_area: Credential exposure via derived sync key
6309fe.evidence: getSyncKey derives favs_<base64(url|user)> with no secret, and saveToCloud publishes favourites/folders to the public store. The record contains only playlist item IDs and folder names — no password — so it is a privacy leak of viewing history, not credential theft. Same root cause as the reported public-store issue; fixing that control covers this surface.

0ddd20.surface: Playlist metadata fields as object keys (category id, React key, favorites identifier, localStorage/progress keys)
0ddd20.risk_area: Prototype pollution / key injection from playlist data
0ddd20.evidence: group-title flows into a `Set`, into `{ id: c, name: c }` objects and into React keys, never through a merge/copy helper. Tested a `group-title="__proto__"` playlist (/workspace/.poc-playlist/proto_test.js): the string is stored as an ordinary Set member and `({}).name` stays undefined, so no prototype is touched. `name` is used only in string concatenation (localStorage keys, episode labels), not as an object path.

ea6cd7.surface: Xtream player_api.php login response -> stored credentials and channel fan-out (App.tsx:1667-1728)
ea6cd7.evidence: Every subsequent request is built from the user-entered base URL plus the user-entered username/password (the `baseUrl`/`userToUse`/`passToUse` locals captured before the response is read); no field of the login JSON is used to choose a host, path prefix or scheme. `user_info.auth === 1` is the only gate on entering the logged-in state — a hostile provider can of course lie, but it is already the operator of the server the user chose.

3c4919.surface: Provider credential-bearing stream URLs in console/ffmpeg argv (src/App.tsx:714/744, electron/main.js:750/812/933-936)
3c4919.risk_area: Credential in logs / process command line
3c4919.evidence: Xtream stream URLs embed user/pass in the path (App.tsx:1688,1701,1713), so when a remote item is transcoded the URL reaches console.log (App.tsx:714/744), the loopback /stream?path= URL, and ffmpeg argv logged at main.js:812 via ffmpeg(videoPath). No log file is written (no createWriteStream/appendFileSync in main.js) — output goes to the parent console only. Not filed as a distinct vulnerability: requires an already-transcoded remote item, exposure is console-only, and process argv is readable only by the same user (Windows does not expose foreign process command lines to other non-admin sessions here). Root cause is the same as vuln-0005; noted as defense-in-depth in its remediation.

bc217d.surface: src/App.tsx logging of credentials (console.error in login/activation handlers)
bc217d.evidence: Activation/login handlers log only a fixed string: App.tsx:1299 console.error('Activation error:', e), :1327 'Save code error:', :1595 'Fetch series info error:', :1642 'M3U Load Error:'. The error objects come from ipcRenderer.invoke rejection, and main.js:661 logs only error.message ('HTTP error! status: N'), never the request URL — so neither xtreamPass nor the KV payload reaches a log via these paths.

f08d66.surface: Referer / URL query-string leakage of provider credentials
f08d66.risk_area: Credential leakage via Referer header or URL
f08d66.evidence: Credentials only appear in URLs sent to the user's own provider (App.tsx:1592,1658,1681,1693,1706,1719-1721) and in stream paths (1688,1701,1713) requested from the same origin. No third-party origin is loaded with a credential-bearing URL in the path, so no cross-origin Referer can carry them; the loopback /stream URL is consumed by the local <video> element only (App.tsx:3979).

775d30.risk_area: DOM XSS / HTML injection from remote telemetry data
775d30.evidence: chart.innerHTML at usage-stats.html:212 interpolates row.date into title="..." (line 216) and into <div class="tick"> (line 218) with no attribute/HTML encoding. Verified in headless Chromium: a row.date of `" x onclick=alert(1) a=` produces a real DOM attribute set [class,title,x,onclick,a] with onclick="alert(1)"; the fix (DOM API + textContent) yields only [class,title]. Reported.

932fff.surface: electron/main.js executeJavaScript window.__initialVideoInfo (argv template literal, lines 511-524 / 597-606)
932fff.evidence: JSON.stringify correctly escapes the four template-literal metacharacters (backtick, ${), plus " and backslash, and emits U+2028/U+2029 as literal ESCAPED chars? Verified by executing the exact template: `C:\v\${...}`, `` C:\v\`+...` ``, `C:\v\";...`, `C:\v\';...`, U+2028, and `</script>` all round-trip as inert string data (marker executions = 0); only the benign filename produced a value. Also no argv input path is attacker-controllable: no custom protocol/deep-link registration, no default-app file-association handling, and media downloads do not supply argv (playback is via file:// / loopback stream URL).

f718ac.evidence: Zero raw-HTML sinks: grep for innerHTML/outerHTML/dangerouslySetInnerHTML/document.write/insertAdjacentHTML/eval/new Function/createContextualFragment/srcDoc/.html( over App.tsx returns 0 hits. All remote IPTV/Xtream/EPG/subtitle/filename values (item.name, item.icon, tvg-logo, epg.current.title/desc, currentCue.text, epg desc) render through React JSX text children or src={item.icon}, which React escapes/validates. Subtitle parsers (parseSRT/VTT/ASS/SUB) strip tags and output is rendered as {currentCue.text}. safeDomId() base64-strips to [A-Za-z0-9]. HLS is loaded via hls.js (no document.write). No window.open/href/target=_blank with user URLs found.

a21f64.risk_area: DOM XSS / dynamic label or href construction
a21f64.evidence: ContextMenu.tsx builds menu items only from the static i18n `t.*` string table (t.play/pause/stop/previous/nextVideo/settings/playlist/exitApp/fullscreen/windowscreen) rendered as React {label} children; no media metadata, no href, no HTML sink. main.tsx is a 10-line createRoot render with no user data.

78dc54.evidence: The policy contains 'unsafe-inline' in default-src and defines no script-src, so inline

04e395.surface: electron/main.js BrowserWindow webPreferences (nodeIntegration/contextIsolation/webSecurity) and navigation controls
04e395.risk_area: Renderer-to-native escalation / navigation to attacker origin
04e395.evidence: Same surface as 70fe0f; resolved and filed as vuln-0008 (critical). The navigation-containment question this row left open was settled by live Electron reproduction: location.href and window.open both escape the app origin while retaining Node, so the missing guard is a real escalation path rather than a theoretical one.

history.evidence: createWindow() (main.js:568-580) sets nodeIntegration:true, contextIsolation:false, webSecurity:false, and neither createWindow nor the stats window in telemetry.js register will-navigate / setWindowOpenHandler / did-create-window. I found no attacker-controllable main-frame navigation in App.tsx (no window.open, location assignment, href, or target=_blank), so I could not demonstrate a navigation primitive; whether one exists via hls.js, the <video>/<source> element or a future UI addition was not established. Node code execution after any renderer script execution is a configuration consequence, not something I exercised.

087d77.risk_area: Navigation / origin escape to attacker-controlled content with Node privileges (RCE)
087d77.evidence: Reproduced in Electron 38.8.6 with the exact webPreferences copy: location.href -> http://127.0.0.1:3111/evil.html navigated the main window (no will-navigate guard present, event observed but no listener cancels it) and the evil page executed require('fs').readFileSync('/etc/hostname'). window.open created a second BrowserWindow whose getLastWebPreferences() = {nodeIntegration:true, contextIsolation:false, webSecurity:false, sandbox:false} and which ran require('os') with the renderer's Node version.

e3d37d.risk_area: Hard-coded credentials / offline cracking and gate bypass impact
e3d37d.evidence: Filed as vuln-0009 (low). Unsalted SHA-256 of the gate username cracked offline to 'ADMIN' from the 14.3M-entry rockyou list; sha256('ADMIN') === GATE_USER_HASH verified. The password digest resisted a rockyou pass with case/leetspeak/suffix mutations, which bounds current crackability but not the design flaw (verifier shipped with the app). safeEqual and isStatsSender ported and unit-checked; the gate protects only aggregate counts plus an owner flag whose sole consumers suppress telemetry pings.

history.evidence: Unsalted SHA-256 of username cracked to 'ADMIN' from the 14.3M-entry rockyou list; sha256('ADMIN') === GATE_USER_HASH verified. safeEqual/crypto.timingSafeEqual branches ported and unit-checked; isStatsSender compares event.sender identity to statsWindow.webContents. Gate unlocks counts only plus owner=true in instance.json (only consumers are sendDailyPing at telemetry.js:101 and the closed handler at :169).

729175.evidence: telemetry:set has no isStatsSender check, but the only effect is writing state.telemetry boolean into instance.json (and cancelling a pending timer). Since app.tsx:1183 invokes it from the main window by design, the missing check grants no capability beyond what the legitimate UI already has; no privilege or data is exposed. Recorded as design weakness only.

6dbf8f.risk_area: Update channel trust / arbitrary code update
6dbf8f.evidence: No setFeedURL/allowPrerelease anywhere in either tree; no package.json/electron-builder config present in the supplied trees, so electron-updater resolves the default GitHub-release provider from the packaged app-update.yml, with NSIS differential signature verification (sha512 + publisherName) enforced by electron-updater. No attacker-reachable code path supplies a feed URL: the updater is only invoked with zero arguments at main.js:539/623. Residual: an attacker who can already write the install directory can edit app-update.yml, which presupposes the FILE_WRITE primitive that the navigation finding already provides, so it is not an independent issue.

1c02a7.surface: electron/usage-stats.html CSP and innerHTML chart rendering (usage-stats.html:5, 212-220)
1c02a7.risk_area: CSP enforcement vs nodeIntegration; HTML injection from counter service
1c02a7.evidence: CSP is default-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' (no script-src, so 'self' governs scripts, unsafe-inline is ignored for script). The page's only script is inline at line 182-250, yet it runs because meta CSP is enforced after parse for the inline script in Chromium/Electron file:// documents in practice — verified by the application functioning; regardless, CSP is irrelevant because line 183 does require('electron') and nodeIntegration:true. The innerHTML sink at 212 interpolates only row.date (toISOString slice from a locally generated array) and row.count (countFrom() enforces typeof number), so no attacker-controlled string reaches it. No injection path found.

28649c.surface: electron/main.js second-instance / did-finish-load argument handling and executeJavaScript (main.js:503-524, 599-609)
28649c.risk_area: Command-line/file-open abuse and JS injection via argv
28649c.evidence: fileArg is taken from commandLine (argv array, no shell involved) filtered by an extension regex, then embedded with JSON.stringify(), which escapes quotes, backslashes and forward slashes so no </script> or ' breakout is possible at the executeJavaScript string boundary. The resulting path is only forwarded to the renderer's file-open handler; path containment is owned by another agent's scope. No argv injection observed.

4453ea.risk_area: Unverified dev-server origin / local port squatting
4453ea.evidence: Only reached when !app.isPackaged, i.e. a developer running from source; shipped builds take the loadFile('dist/index.html') branch. A local process binding :3000 before the dev server is a developer-machine scenario with no delivered impact, and the developer already has code execution. Recorded for completeness, not as a finding.

09d28e.evidence: Only autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required, enable-features=PlatformHEVCDecoderSupport and disable-features=HardwareMediaKeyHandling are appended. None weaken origin, sandbox or TLS enforcement; no remote-debugging-port, no disable-web-security, no ignore-certificate-errors.

ed1257.surface: electron/telemetry.js openStatsWindow() webPreferences and statistics window navigation (telemetry.js:150-173)
ed1257.risk_area: Node integration in a second window with no navigation guard
ed1257.evidence: The statistics window uses nodeIntegration:true, contextIsolation:false with no preload and no navigation guard, the same posture as the main window. It is not an independent exploitable route, though: it loads a fixed local file (usage-stats.html) and the only remote influence is JSON from the counter service, which is rendered with textContent and an innerHTML sink constrained to numbers and generated dates (see the CSP/innerHTML entry). No attacker-controlled string reaches a script sink in that document. The defect is the shared preference pattern, which is already reported for the main window (vuln-0008) and whose multi-part fix covers both windows; recorded here so the duplicate posture is documented rather than silently missed.

10aa31.surface: src/App.tsx activation-code sharing namespace (KV_APP_KEY / handleCreateCode / handleActivationLogin)
10aa31.risk_area: Cross-user credential disclosure via an unauthenticated datastore
10aa31.evidence: Already reported as vuln-0005 by another agent. Independently confirmed by a read-only full-keyspace sweep of the live store: 21 populated records retrieved with no authentication, including a provider credential set; unpopulated codes return "". Added the measured population and the no-real-victim-data note to that finding via update_vulnerability_report rather than filing a duplicate.

3bb844.surface: Electron IPC handler inventory across main.js and telemetry.js (no sender/origin authorization on any handler)
3bb844.risk_area: Missing IPC sender authorization / confused deputy
3bb844.evidence: All 13 handlers were enumerated: quit-app, restart-and-install, iptv-fetch, get-network-info, get-stream-url, cancel-seek-optimize, probe-seek-quality, optimize-for-seeking, extract-seek-frame, telemetry:get, telemetry:set, creator-stats:login, creator-stats:load. Only the two creator-stats handlers call isStatsSender(); the rest accept any sender. Under the current single-window design this is not an independent finding — the sole application window legitimately needs all of them, and the renderer already holds Node privileges by design so a sender check would add nothing. The impact only becomes real once a foreign origin can occupy a window, which is the reported navigation defect (vuln-0008); the durable fix there is removing nodeIntegration plus a preload allowlist rather than adding per-handler sender checks. iptv-fetch SSRF and the ffmpeg file-path handlers are owned by other agents.

82a7b1.risk_area: Cross-user data disclosure and tampering via a derivable identifier
82a7b1.evidence: Filed as vuln-0010 (medium, confidence medium). getSyncKey is a pure function of provider URL+username with no secret; reproduced the derivation in Node and showed a stranger lands on the owner's identifier. Store read authorization absent confirmed live on the same namespace. Gap: no populated favourites record was located, so the population of that record family is unquantified.
